question: What does medication non-compliance mean in nursing care?

options.A: Failing to follow a prescribed treatment plan
options.B: Sleeping through scheduled hospital visiting hours
options.C: Refusing to pay hospital bills after discharge
options.D: Buying drugs from unregistered local chemist shops

explanation: Non-compliance occurs when patients do not take their medicines as directed by healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do patients often give misleading answers when asked about taking their medications?

options.A: To please the nurse and avoid scolding
options.B: To hide symptoms of a new infectious disease
options.C: To test the clinical knowledge of the nurse
options.D: To purposely sell their drugs for quick cash

explanation: Patients frequently report full compliance simply to avoid disappointing their healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is primary medication non-adherence?

options.A: The patient never fills the initial prescription
options.B: The patient stops taking drugs after feeling better
options.C: The patient forgets the evening dose of medication
options.D: The patient reduces the drug dose on their own

explanation: Primary non-adherence happens right at the start when a patient leaves the clinic but never obtains the prescribed drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h2)

question: A patient stops taking antibiotics early because the fever has gone down. What pattern is this?

options.A: Erratic scheduling due to a busy work routine
options.B: Intelligent adjustment based on drug cost
options.D: Primary failure to obtain the prescription

explanation: Stopping medication before the full course finishes, simply because symptoms disappear, is premature discontinuation. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is a major financial barrier to drug compliance in Nigeria?

options.B: Free pharmacy services in all rural areas

explanation: Most patients pay directly for their drugs, which leads to rationing when finances become tight. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h3)

question: How do traditional and herbal remedies often affect orthodox drug adherence?

options.A: They reduce the financial burden of hospital stays
options.B: They always improve the speed of wound healing
options.C: They can conflict with prescribed medical treatments
options.D: They guarantee patients will take their clinic drugs

explanation: Using herbal mixtures alongside hospital medicines often leads to dangerous interactions or causes patients to abandon orthodox drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is a direct clinical result of chronic drug non-compliance?

options.B: Permanent immunity against high blood pressure
options.C: Reduced need for future medical checkups

explanation: Skipping medications for chronic illnesses leads to poorly controlled disease and severe health complications. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h4)

question: How does poor medication adherence affect the broader healthcare system?

options.A: It saves money by reducing pharmacy inventory needs
options.B: It decreases waiting times in outpatient clinics
options.C: It eliminates the need for diagnostic laboratory tests
options.D: It increases emergency hospital admissions and costs

explanation: Patients who do not take their drugs eventually return sicker, requiring costly emergency interventions and longer hospital stays. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is an indirect way nurses can assess medication adherence?

options.A: Conducting pill counts during home visits
options.B: Observing the patient swallow morning doses
options.C: Listening to patient promises at discharge
options.D: Asking patients if they take drugs every day

explanation: Counting remaining pills in a container helps nurses see if the patient is taking the correct amount of medication. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is a non-judgmental approach important when asking about missed doses?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from changing the prescription
options.B: It stops the patient from asking about drug costs
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never miss a dose
options.D: It encourages the patient to tell the truth

explanation: Patients hide missed doses when they fear scolding or punishment from healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is a practical method to help patients remember their medication schedule?

options.A: Instructing the patient to hide all pill bottles
options.B: Stopping education until the disease worsens
options.C: Matching dosing times to daily routines
options.D: Giving long lists of complex medical terms

explanation: Tying medication times to daily habits like eating meals helps patients remember to take their drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why should nurses involve family caregivers in medication counselling?

options.A: To provide extra support and supervision at home
options.B: To shift all nursing responsibilities to relatives
options.C: To ensure the family pays for hospital bills
options.D: To prevent the patient from asking questions

explanation: Family members can help remind patients, manage refills, and monitor adherence outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which professional can help organize complex drug regimens into weekly blister packs?
explanation: Pharmacists play a key role in dispensing and organizing medicines into easy-to-use formats like blister packs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of a multidisciplinary team in managing non-compliance?

options.A: It makes hospital administration run without any paper records
options.B: It addresses both medical and social causes of poor adherence
options.C: It ensures that nurses do all the patient teaching alone
options.D: It eliminates the need for follow-up clinic appointments

explanation: Different professionals bring unique skills, from medical adjustment to social support, to tackle the root causes of non-compliance. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h7)
